chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn al-Qasim (al-Qasim) who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the night in which what is sought is sought, when is the bath (ghusl)? So he (peace be upon him) said: From the beginning of the night; and if you wish, when you stand (for prayer) at its end. And I asked him about the standing (for prayer), so he said: You stand in its beginning and its end.

key_terms.اللَّيْلَةِ: The night (specifically referring to the night of the 15th of Sha'ban)

ai.seo_question: When should one perform the ritual bath and night prayer on the 15th of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in performing the ritual bath (*ghusl*) for Laylat al-Bara'ah, allowing it at the onset of night or deferred until the time of rising for prayer. It further establishes the practice of *Qiyam* (night vigil) as a continuous act of worship spanning both the early and late portions of the night, reflecting the Shia emphasis on prolonged devotion and spiritual preparation during this auspicious occasion.
